title: Reflective presheaf presentation of a presentable infinity category
statement:
Use the infinity categories and nested universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U\prime$ of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], and the coherent functor and mapping-space conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Small means $\mathcal U$-small, and $\mathcal S$ denotes the infinity category of small spaces. Let $\mathcal C$ be a presentable infinity category. There exist a small infinity category $D$, its presheaf infinity category $\mathcal P=\operatorname{Fun}(D^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$, and functors $L:\mathcal P\to\mathcal C$ and $i:\mathcal C\to\mathcal P$ such that $i$ is fully faithful and there is a coherent mapping-space adjunction
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(LX,c)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(X,i(c))$$
natural in $X\in\mathcal P$ and $c\in\mathcal C$. Its unit $\eta:\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal P}\to iL$ and counit $\epsilon:Li\to\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal C}$ satisfy the triangle identities, and $\epsilon$ is a natural equivalence. The functor $L$ preserves all small colimits, and $L(\eta_X)$ is an equivalence for every $X$. For every $X\in\mathcal P$ and $c\in\mathcal C$, precomposition with the unit gives an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(iLX,ic)\xrightarrow{\ \eta_X^*\ }\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(X,ic).$$

source.place: Theorem 5.5.1.1, implication (1) to (5), printed pp. 457-460; Definition 5.2.7.2 (localization means fully faithful right adjoint) and Proposition 5.2.3.5. The unit, counit and displayed precomposition formula spell out the reflective adjunction Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks Project tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Unpack presentability using [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Choose an infinite regular cardinal $\kappa\in\mathcal U$ and an essentially small full subcategory of $\kappa$-compact generators. Call this subcategory $A$, choose an equivalence $e:D\to A$ from a small quasicategory, and write $f:D\to\mathcal C$ for its composite with the full inclusion. If $q:I\to A$ presents an object, choose a quasi-inverse $r:A\to D$ and put $p=rq$; the equivalence $er\simeq\operatorname{id}_A$ identifies $fp$ with the original diagram in $\mathcal C$ and identifies their cocones, so the same colimit is obtained. Full faithfulness of the inclusion and of $e$ makes $f$ fully faithful, and its values are $\kappa$-compact because they lie in $A$. Thus every $c\in\mathcal C$ has a specified small $\kappa$-filtered presentation $c\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{a\in I}f(p(a))$ with $p:I\to D$. Here only a presentation of the particular object under consideration is chosen; the functors below are not defined by making unrelated choices of such presentations. The category $\mathcal C$ is locally small and has all small colimits, including the empty colimit.

source.place: Definition 5.5.0.1; accessibility convention of Proposition 5.4.2.2. Agent argument from compact generators, for the conclusion of Theorem 5.5.1.1(5).

proof.text: Put $\mathcal P=\operatorname{Fun}(D^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$ and $j(d)=\operatorname{Map}_D(-,d)$. Construct $i$ by composing the coherent Yoneda functor of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] for $\mathcal C$ with restriction along $f^{\mathrm{op}}$. In particular $i(c)(d)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(f(d),c)$ is a small space, and full faithfulness of $f$ gives a coherent equivalence $if\simeq j$.

source.place: Theorem 5.5.1.1(1) to (5), restricted Yoneda construction; Proposition 5.1.3.1.

proof.text: Let $q:I\to\mathcal C$ be a small $\kappa$-filtered diagram with a colimiting cocone to $c$. For $d\in D$ put $H_d(a)=i(q(a))(d)$ and $M_d=i(c)(d)$, with their induced cocone. Each $f(d)$ is $\kappa$-compact, so [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category] says that this mapping-space cocone is colimiting in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'}$. Its individual spaces have small representatives because $\mathcal C$ is locally small.

source.place: Definition 5.3.4.5 and the compactness convention of def-coef-presentable-infinity-category.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-universe-colimit-descent] to $H_d\to\Delta_I M_d$. It supplies a colimit $Q_d$ in small spaces and shows that the induced comparison $Q_d\to M_d$ is an equivalence, so this cocone is colimiting in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$. This holds for every $d$. The pointwise criterion in [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], with the small parameter $D^{\mathrm{op}}$, now shows that $iq\to i(c)$ is colimiting in $\mathcal P$. Thus $i$ preserves small $\kappa$-filtered colimits; small throughout means $\mathcal U$-small.

source.place: Agent universe-descent argument extracted from original step 2; pointwise colimit criterion of Proposition 5.1.2.2.

proof.text:
Fix $c,c'\in\mathcal C$ and use a presentation $c\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{a\in I}f(p(a))$ from step 1. Step 4 gives $ic\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{a\in I}j(p(a))$. The colimit mapping-space test of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] in $\mathcal P$ and in $\mathcal C$, together with [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-evaluation], gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(ic,ic')\simeq\lim_{a\in I^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(j(p(a)),ic')\simeq\lim_{a\in I^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(f(p(a)),c')\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,c').$$
This identifies the actual map induced by $i$ as an equivalence: at each $p(a)$, evaluation at its identity sends the transformation induced by $u:c\to c'$ to the composite $f(p(a))\to c\xrightarrow{u}c'$. These are exactly the components of the colimit comparison on the right, including their coherent compatibilities. Hence the map on the entire mapping space, rather than just on components, is inverted by the displayed chain. This proves full faithfulness of $i$. Every limit here is indexed by the small $I^{\mathrm{op}}$.

source.place: Theorem 5.5.1.1(1) to (5), agent expansion via restricted Yoneda; Propositions 5.1.3.1-5.1.3.2 and Lemma 5.1.5.2 supply the mapping-space tests.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-free-cocompletion], $\mathcal P$ has small mapping spaces and all small colimits. Apply its restriction equivalence with target $\mathcal C$ to the functor $f$. This gives a coherent functor $L:\mathcal P\to\mathcal C$, preserving every small colimit, and a coherent natural equivalence $Lj\simeq f$. Thus the colimit-preservation assertion of the item already holds. This construction uses the full free-cocompletion equivalence, not the adjoint functor theorem for presentable categories.

source.place: Theorem 5.1.5.6; construction of the colimit extension of the compact-generator inclusion.

proof.text: For $c\in\mathcal C$ compare the contravariant space-valued functors $K_c(X)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(LX,c)$ and $R_c(X)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(X,ic)$. They take small colimits to limits by step 6 and [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. On $j(D)$ their restrictions are naturally equivalent: $K_c(jd)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(f(d),c)=ic(d)\simeq R_c(jd)$ by $Lj\simeq f$ and [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-evaluation]. Since $\mathcal S$ has small limits by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], its opposite has small colimits. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-free-cocompletion] with target $\mathcal S^{\mathrm{op}}$ to $K_c^{\mathrm{op}},R_c^{\mathrm{op}}:\mathcal P\to\mathcal S^{\mathrm{op}}$. A quasi-inverse to its restriction equivalence lifts the equivalence just obtained, giving $K_c\simeq R_c$. This lift is coherent in $c$ as well as $X$: apply that same quasi-inverse to the diagram of restrictions parametrized by $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$, and compose with its two inverse-functor equivalences. Postcomposition by a quasi-inverse is defined on diagrams and all their simplices, so the equivalence is one of mapping-space bifunctors. One may use an additional ambient universe for this parameter functor category without changing $D$, the spaces, or the meaning of small. No limit indexed by the large $\mathcal P$ or $\mathcal C$ is used.

source.place: Theorem 5.1.5.6 with opposite target; Propositions 5.1.3.1-5.1.3.2 and Lemma 5.1.5.2. Agent construction of the natural adjunction equivalence.

proof.text: Step 7 represents, for each $c$, the presheaf $X\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(LX,c)$ by $ic$. By [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-adjoint-criterion] there is a coherent right adjoint $r$ to $L$ and its representing mapping-space bifunctor equivalence. Composing it with step 7 gives $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(-,r(c))\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(-,i(c))$, coherently in $c$.

source.place: Proposition 5.2.4.2 and Section 5.2, pointwise representability criterion.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], the Yoneda functor $j_{\mathcal P}$ is fully faithful; $\mathcal P$ has small mapping spaces by step 6. Step 8 gives an equivalence $j_{\mathcal P}r\simeq j_{\mathcal P}i$ in the functor category with parameter $\mathcal C$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-functor-equivalence-lift], enlarging the ambient universe to contain the presheaf target, to obtain $r\simeq i$ coherently, inducing that same Yoneda-image equivalence. Transport the adjunction along it to obtain $L\dashv i$, with the unit, counit and triangle identities supplied by [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-adjoint-criterion]. Naturality and the images of identity maps give the forward formula $h\mapsto i(h)\eta_X$ and inverse formula $g\mapsto\epsilon_cL(g)$.

source.place: Agent functor-level Yoneda lifting extracted from original step 6; Section 5.2, units and counits.

proof.text: For each $c,c'\in\mathcal C$, precomposition by $\epsilon_c:Lic\to c$ is an equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,c')\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(Lic,c')$. Indeed, under the adjunction its value at $h$ is $i(h\epsilon_c)\eta_{ic}\simeq i(h)$ by the triangle identity $i(\epsilon_c)\eta_{ic}\simeq1_{ic}$; the map $h\mapsto i(h)$ is an equivalence by step 5. Taking $c'=Lic$ supplies $t:c\to Lic$ with $t\epsilon_c\simeq1_{Lic}$. The two maps $\epsilon_ct$ and $1_c$ have homotopic images under precomposition by $\epsilon_c$; using the same equivalence with $c'=c$ yields $\epsilon_ct\simeq1_c$. Thus every counit component is an equivalence, with an explicit two-sided inverse. The counit is already a coherent transformation by step 9. Apply the vertexwise-equivalence clause of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] with $K=\mathcal C$, using $\mathcal U\prime$ as that clause's small universe and one further ambient universe. The parameter and target $\mathcal C$ fit in $\mathcal U\prime$; this application does not change the original meaning of small colimits or spaces. This makes $\epsilon$ a natural equivalence, as required.

source.place: Section 5.2.7, reflective adjunction; explicit inverse argument from steps 3 and 6.

proof.text:
The other triangle identity is $\epsilon_{LX}L(\eta_X)\simeq1_{LX}$. Since $\epsilon_{LX}$ is an equivalence by step 10, $L(\eta_X)$ is its inverse and is therefore an equivalence. Finally full faithfulness in step 5 and the adjunction in step 9 identify the composite
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(iLX,ic)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(LX,c)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(X,ic)$$
with precomposition by $\eta_X$: a map $i(h)$ is sent to $i(h)\eta_X$, and every map on the left is so represented on its full mapping space. This is an equivalence and gives the displayed unit-precomposition assertion. Along with steps 5, 6, 9 and 10 this proves every clause of the item.

source.place: Definition 5.2.7.2 and the triangle identities; explicit unit-precomposition calculation.
